title: Vetala Extended Tale 90: The Two Sisters and the Golden Loom

full_text:
Under the dim moon, Vikram hoisted the Vetala again. The ghost began:

"Two sisters, Vasundhara and Priyamvada, were the master weavers of the city. Vasundhara possessed an unparalleled talent for spinning delicate silk threads of unmatched strength, but lacked eye for color. Priyamvada possessed an extraordinary genius for blending vibrant natural dyes, but lacked patience for spinning fine yarn.

For years, they competed bitterly, each producing flawed tapestries and bad-mouthing the other. At last, an old grandmother intervened: 'Why compete in imperfection when you could combine your gifts into perfection?'

The sisters embraced in reconciliation. Together, they produced a royal coronation canopy of such luminous strength and sublime color that it became the pride of the realm.

Tell me, Vikram: what unlocked their genius—their individual mastery or their reconciliation?"

King Vikramaditya answered: "Reconciliation unlocked their genius. Individual talent without harmony remains incomplete and frustrated. When humility dissolves pride and unites complementary gifts, human creativity reaches its highest glory."

"Sharp and true!" laughed the Vetala, and darted back to the tree.
moral: Harmony of differing talents achieves masterpieces that isolated pride can never touch.
